title: Security risks sketchbook — Z. Patel
content:
Purpose: brain-dump of risks, quick control mapping ideas, and shallow test scenarios for SOC2 preflight. This is informal — working notes for myself and a couple teammates.

Top-level risk hypotheses (raw):
- Data isolation gaps on Dedicated/Private: config drift might cause cross-tenant access during autoscaling or failed deprovision flows.
- KV/prefix cache leakage: cached prefix or KV-store entries could be served to an incorrect tenant if eviction or cache-key normalization fails.
- Model variant fallback audit gap: automatic routing/fallback to cheaper model variants can lose provenance (which model served which response) unless we log variant_id and model_hash for every request.
- Key management: rotation procedures for customer-managed KMS in Private deployments are under-documented; unclear recovery steps if rotation fails mid-deploy.
- Console RBAC: role granularity in Redwood Console is coarse; need separation for "deploy" vs "billing/view" vs "rollout-control".
- Observability retention & PII: traces and prompt logs kept for X days, but prompt redaction rules are applied inconsistently across hosted vs private.

Quick control-mapping sketches (control -> owner -> gap / question):
- Access reviews (monthly) -> prod-iam -> gap: no automated evidence export; rely on console screenshots. Q: can we script full export of role assignments for SOC evidence?
- Change control for serving runtime (PR -> canary -> release) -> release-engineering -> gap: release checklist not mandatory for infra-only changes. Q: add policy to require rollouts for kernel changes?
- Encryption-in-transit checks -> infra -> gap: 3rd party load-balancer configs for some private customers not validated in our runbook.
- Backup & restore for model artifacts -> platform-engineering -> gap: restore DR test cadence unclear for deduplicated model store.

Candidate test ideas (fast, do in a day or two):
- Ad-hoc access log reconciliation: pick 5 users, reconcile console roles with IAM export, note discrepancies.
- Small chaos simulation: simulate a GPU pool scale-down to observe routing fallback and verify telemetry includes model_variant, model_hash, region, request_id.
- KV cache boundary test: issue interleaved requests across two tenants with identical prefix tokens; verify responses include tenant_id in logs and no cross-tenant hits in cache telemetry.
- KMS failover walk-through: emulate key rotation error on a staging private deploy and step through runbook. Record gaps.

Evidence artifacts we probably need (thinking aloud):
- Automated role assignment exports (CSV) for last 6 months.
- Runbooks and last-executed timestamps for restore/rotation/scale ops.
- Request-level logs with model_id/model_hash/variant_id + tenant_id + request_id for last 30 days.
- Redaction rules config and sample prompt artifacts showing redaction working end-to-end.

Open questions / conversation starters with teams:
- Serving-runtime: can we add model_hash to all fallback logs? Effort estimate? (ping @liam)
- Console: exportable monthly access report? (ping @nia)
- Private deployments: how many customers use customer-managed KMS vs our KMS? Do we have SLAs for rotation success?

Notes to self (todo queue):
- [ ] Draft 1-pager for SOC auditor on "routing + fallback provenance" with sample logs.
- [ ] File a ticket to instrument model_hash in fallback path (SEC-432 linked above).
- [ ] Run KV cache boundary test on staging cluster next Wed.
- [ ] Ask SRE for last 3 incident runbooks that involved autoscaling and capture any tenants impacted.

Small heuristics/observations from running tests last quarter: 
- When we enabled prefix caching in early prod, we saw a 3–5% increase in wrong-cache-hit telemetry in week-1; root cause turned out to be a normalization bug for trailing whitespace in prompt keys. Worth adding normalization tests to unit suite.
- Customers on Dedicated sometimes configure custom load-balancers; our docs assume a passthrough TLS config — need a checklist entry for private LB validation during onboarding.

Useful links / quick refs:
- SOC2 readiness confluence (high level): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/SOC2+Readiness+Plan
- Related Jira: SEC-432 (instrument model provenance), SEC-410 (KMS rotation runbook), ENG-901 (kb: cache normalization test additions)

Closing thought: keep this as a messy log. The goal is to capture hypotheses and quick tests I can hand off to SRE/release-engineering for concrete tickets. Will refine after next sync with Liam and Nia.

-- zara
